adjudications.claimedSuppressor: KI#2 (integer-division dust always rounds DOWN, in protocol's favor)
adjudications.reasoning: KI#2 is a statement about the DIRECTION of a rounding error and about who retains the dust. It is a value-accounting disposition: the protocol keeps the crumbs. DEDUP-001 is an AVAILABILITY defect: a batch reverts atomically, and layer (ii) is a PERMANENT wedge in which the dust user can never be batch-migrated and finalizeAndReset stays blocked until that user voluntarily self-exits. KI#2 says nothing about revert behaviour, batch atomicity, or terminal-migration liveness. Worse for the suppression argument: KI#2's 'in protocol's favor' framing PRESUMES the dust is silently retained — here it is not retained, it detonates the transaction. The known issue describes the benign case and this is the case where the benign assumption fails.
adjudications.precedent: Prior runs already drew exactly this line for the sibling finding bf5018deab ('distinct from KI#2'), which is the same root-cause class on InPlaceMigrator._reinjectWithTopup. Suppressing DEDUP-001 under KI#2 would contradict a standing adjudication.

adjudications.claimedSuppressor: KI#7 (replacing an in-use yield strategy does not auto-migrate funds out of the old one)
adjudications.verdict: NOT SUPPRESSED — clean miss on three independent grounds

reasoning.ground1_direction: KI#7 governs funds LEFT BEHIND in the OLD strategy when it is replaced — a source-side FAILURE TO EVACUATE. DEDUP-002 is the opposite vector: idle balance swept FORWARD INTO the NEW strategy (src/StableStaker.sol:271-274, idleBalance = IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this)), bounded by the RAW TOKEN BALANCE and by nothing else) which totalStaked never accounts for. No reading of 'does not auto-migrate funds OUT OF THE OLD ONE' extends to a sweep INTO the new one. The text does not cover the forward direction, and the task explicitly required me to say so if it did not: it does not.
reasoning.ground2_precondition_inversion: This is the decisive point. KI#7's hazard requires an IN-USE (non-empty) strategy — that is the literal subject of the sentence. DEDUP-002 fires precisely when totalStaked == 0, i.e. in the state KI#7 NAMES AS THE SAFE BRANCH ('replace only while totalStaked == 0'). KI#7 prescribes as its REMEDY the exact condition under which DEDUP-002 occurs. A known issue cannot suppress a defect located inside its own recommended safe harbour; doing so would convert the mitigation advice into a blanket immunity for the mitigation's own failure mode.
reasoning.ground3_no_authority: Per the provenance check above, KI#7 does not re-derive from CLAUDE.md at HEAD at all. Its disjunction has been replaced by a hard require at src/StableStaker.sol:236. Even if grounds 1 and 2 were arguable, an un-re-derivable cached item carries no suppression authority.

adjudications.mechanismConfirmedInSource: Verified by direct read: setYieldStrategy gates on totalStaked == 0 (:236) — which PINS totalStaked at zero — then sweeps the unconditional raw balance into the new strategy (:271-274). initiateMigration later calls _routeExit(token, P = totalStaked) and post-checks require(strategy.principalOf(token, address(this)) == 0, 'StableStaker: incomplete exit') (:457-460). With strategy principal > totalStaked the exit under-drains by construction and the post-check can never be satisfied. Permanent.

adjudications.verdict: NOT SUPPRESSED — independently verified, not taken on assertion
verificationPerformed: grep -ni 'fee|transferFee|FeeOnTransfer|rebase|blacklist|weird|USDT' over the PoC => ZERO hits.
Token under test is a plain MockERC20('USD Coin','USDC',6) with no transfer hook.

RE-RAN the suite myself rather than trusting the upstream agent's claim (project memory: subagent tool output is not evidence): 5 passed, 0 failed, 8.70ms.
adjudications.rootCauseIsNotFoT: The zero destination credit arises from ERC4626 SHARE-PRICE ROUNDING on the destination (1 wei of USDC into a vault at price 1.05 mints 0 shares, so _routeDeposit returns 0 and depositFor's require(credited > 0) at src/StableStaker.sol:640 reverts). That is integer division against a share price, not a transfer fee. The FoT carve-out is inapplicable on the mechanism, not merely unnecessary.

adjudications.claimedSuppressor: KI#4 / KI#5 (yield stays protocol-owned; exits forward ACTUAL while accounting decrements REQUESTED)
adjudications.reasoning: KI#4 and KI#5 describe what the protocol DOES, and both re-derive cleanly at HEAD. They therefore do carry authority over the underlying CODE behaviour — which is exactly why the code defect is NOT being filed as new this run: it stays owned by open Low 4f143a9573 via ledger-hygiene request LH-01 (scope-extend, do not mint a new fingerprint). What DEDUP-005 files is the DOCUMENTATION MIS-ATTRIBUTION, and a known issue cannot sanitize a FALSE STATEMENT ABOUT ITSELF. NatSpec section (E) scopes the shortfall to an underwater SOURCE and asserts 'This contract redeposits exactly what it received and no more' as if that were exhaustive; the destination-side haircut is independent of source health and bites in full on a perfectly healthy migration. An operator reading (E) concludes 'healthy source => no user loss', which is false. KI#5 makes the haircut a known BEHAVIOUR; it does not make the contract's misdescription of that behaviour a known issue.
adjudications.projectLaw: In-source NatSpec carries no suppression authority, and a falsely-exhaustive doc block RAISES severity rather than lowering it. Story-018's test plan repeats the same conflation (describing MockYieldStrategy.setDepositSlippageBps as 'how underwater conditions are simulated'), so the healthy-source-plus-haircutting-destination case is unmodeled by the story AND by the test suite.
adjudications.severityInputNotSuppressionBasis: The reachCaveat (≈zero on the currently-wired direct ERC4626 route; exposure latent until a market/AMM-backed destination is wired) is a legitimate input to the severity-classifier. It is NOT a sanitization basis and was not treated as one.

reasoning.whatIsSurprising_andThereforeInScope: The finding is not 'it is one-way'. It is that the SOURCE is frozen irreversibly with ZERO on-chain validation of the DESTINATION. CLAUDE.md:52-53 enumerates real destination preconditions — both sides must have setMigrator, the new staker must have the token registered via addToken, and the new staker must be a phUSD minter — as a PROSE DEPLOYMENT CHECKLIST, while the code checks none of them before the irreversible step. The owner's surprise is 'it let me fire the one-way door while the destination was unwired', and that is a consequence a competent operator would not predict from reading either the code or the runbook.

regressionAnalysisDetail.priorTitle: Underwater buffer-path withdraw desyncs totalStaked < strategy.principalOf, making initiateMigration's post-check unsatisfiable — terminal migration permanently un-initiable
regressionAnalysisDetail.SANITIZER_RECALL_GAP_CLOSED: The deduplicator adjudicated DEDUP-002 against 678e6fa2, dab5a656, dbdc3ac9b9, 969722dc9e and b197e829 — but NOT against dc361b7d, which is the single closest entry in the entire ledger. Adjudicated here rather than left unexamined.
regressionAnalysisDetail.verdict: NOT A REGRESSION — but a RE-EMERGENCE OF A CLOSED DEFECT CLASS through a new producer. Own bucket.
regressionAnalysisDetail.reasoning: IDENTICAL SYMPTOM: strategy.principalOf > totalStaked => _routeExit(P = totalStaked) under-drains => require(principalOf == 0, 'StableStaker: incomplete exit') can never be satisfied => the token can never enter terminal migration. Same line, same revert string, same permanent-availability impact. DIFFERENT PRODUCER of the desync: dc361b7d's producer was an underwater buffer-path withdraw decrementing totalStaked without touching strategy principal (fixed by story-007's relinquishPrincipal reconciliation). DEDUP-002's producer is setYieldStrategy sweeping unmatched idle balance INTO the strategy, incrementing strategy principal without touching totalStaked. Opposite legs of the same inequality.
regressionAnalysisDetail.priorPatchVerifiedIntact: story-007's fix is PRESENT and UNMODIFIED at HEAD: src/StableStaker.sol:796 `strategy.relinquishPrincipal(token, amount)` in the underwater buffer branch. Confirmed by direct read. No restoration is owed and NOBODY should be sent to restore an intact patch — that is the precise error this adjudication exists to prevent (cf. the expired-closure-vs-regression memo).
regressionAnalysisDetail.precedentForKeepingSeparate: The ledger already set this precedent explicitly: dc361b7d itself records 'Distinct upstream cause and code location from acknowledged 3d61c955 (migrateOut) — shared SYMPTOM only, NOT merged, to avoid burying a live liveness defect (Law 1).' Applying the same rule, DEDUP-002 is correctly a NEW entry with a distinct rootCauseClass.
regressionAnalysisDetail.WHY_THIS_RAISES_THE_STAKES: This is a severity input the severity-classifier MUST see. DEDUP-002's exact impact — permanently un-initiable terminal migration for a token — was already assessed once by this project as a MEDIUM and was considered serious enough to warrant a dedicated story (story-007) and a dedicated fix. DEDUP-002 reproduces that impact by another route. Any argument that DEDUP-002 is 'only' a Low must explain why the identical impact was a Medium in run-07.

regressionAnalysisDetail.verdict: NOT A REGRESSION, NOT AN INCOMPLETE FIX — a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of a fix that is working correctly
regressionAnalysisDetail.reasoning: Both prior entries were closed by story-011 ADDING require(credited > 0) to depositFor. That guard is present and correct at src/StableStaker.sol:640, and the defects it closed genuinely cannot recur: no zero-credit phantom staker can be inserted into _stakers. DEDUP-001 does not allege the guard is missing, wrong, or bypassed — it alleges that CrossVersionMigrator (a contract that did not exist when either entry was filed) ships its OWN skip-guard `if (amounts[i] > 0)` that reads the SOURCE credit while the revert fires on the DESTINATION credit. The story-011 guard is the thing correctly reverting; the new contract's guard is the thing reading the wrong quantity. An incomplete-fix classification would wrongly imply story-011's patch is defective. It is not.
regressionAnalysisDetail.structuralParallel: This is the same shape as DEDUP-002 vs the empty-pool gate: a correct fix, landed on the evergreen contract, whose consequences were not re-derived when a NEW contract was written against it. Two independent instances of that pattern in one run is itself worth the report-writer's attention.
